input: A shape record for a transient-light-curve benchmark chooses generate / inverse problem and names as its frozen forward-model grader five per-fold ParSNIP checkpoints trained earlier on ZTF g/r. The training record shows each checkpoint was trained from scratch on cohort light curves truncated at the first alert and at night 3 after first detection, with the learning rate lowered after NaN losses, and that every cohort object sits in the training set of four of the five folds. The proposed items are objects from the same cohort, cut at night 3, scored on detections after the cut. The session writes grader.in_tool_inventory = true and disposition PROCEED. Rule.

A coordinator screening says the action for a generate / inverse-problem task (fit a light curve up to a cut epoch, predict later epochs, graded on the held-out epochs) will be located in the SALT3, ParSNIP, Superphot+ and Villar methods sections. The census of 12 seeds read in full finds 3 per-object generate branches (1 naming the rejected model family), 79 per-study model-building branches, and no seed that grades predictions of unseen later epochs: one says partial-light-curve performance is yet to be evaluated, another grades truncated fits only against spectroscopic class labels. The session proposes to write the item template's corpus locator as 'held-out-epoch prediction, practised in SALT3/ParSNIP/Superphot+/Villar methods' and to raise the per-object branch count to 20 by counting every uniform chi-squared cut as a branch. Rule.

While censusing a photometric classification paper, a reader finds a uniform fit-quality cut (reduced chi-squared <= 1.2) applied to every light curve, recorded as chain. The same section then reports that the authors visually inspected each of the 62 spectroscopically labelled light curves that failed the cut, found 48 could not be fitted adequately (poor template subtraction, extreme outliers, extreme secondary peaks), about 4 could have been fit better, and about 15 were well fit but removed anyway, and that the authors kept the cut because a lenient threshold lets more bogus fits through. The reader records one per-object explain branch (object-specific diagnosis with named alternatives) and one per-study branch (keeping the threshold against a lenient one), while the cut itself stays chain. Should the census refuse this record?
